gaps.sentence: 'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
gaps.explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.

gaps.sentence: 'The shop closes at six,' she reminded me. She reminded me that the shop ___ at six.
gaps.explanation: Even habitual present simple backshifts after a past reporting verb: closes → closed.

gaps.sentence: 'Please don't smoke in here,' the host said. The host asked me ___ in there.
gaps.explanation: Negative requests: asked me not to smoke; 'here' shifts to 'there'.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't leave your belongings unattended,' the announcement repeated. The announcement ___ passengers not to leave their belongings unattended.
gaps.hint: warn sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: The warning fits warn + object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' he said. He said he would see me ___.
gaps.explanation: Time expressions shift: tomorrow becomes the next day / the following day.

gaps.sentence: 'You should apply for the grant,' he told me. He ___ me to apply for the grant.
gaps.explanation: Advice is reported as advise + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: The hijackers ___ to blow up the plane unless their demands were met.
gaps.explanation: A declared harmful action is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.
